# ATILF — TLFi, regard

ATILF. *Trésor de la langue française informatisé*, s.v. “regard,” Étymologie et histoire. CNRTL. Consulted 8 September 2026. Cite the actual online entry; the portal’s copyright date does not date composition of each dictionary statement.

The entry **sources** the French branch of [E2’s Regard operation](../../../../etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md). English borrowing and Anglo-French history require their own witnesses.

<a id="passages"></a>
## Lexical witness

<a id="atilf-tlfi-regard-q001"></a>
### q001 — Looking, attention and administrative inspection

**Paraphrase:** the entry treats *regard* as derived from *regarder* and dates ocular use to the late tenth century, attentive regard to the first half of the twelfth, inspection to 1262 and administrative control to 1464. It also records an opening for inspecting a fountain’s interior in 1580.

**Locator:** s.v. regard, Étymologie et histoire, full etymology section

**Verification:** [CNRTL, regard, Étymologie et histoire](https://www.cnrtl.fr/etymologie/regard), full etymology section read 2026-09-08. The medieval and early modern editions cited there remain dictionary-mediated witnesses. These differentiated uses develop the French historical branch; they do not prove Taylor’s Con-text-through-Diaphaneity relation or supply an English first-use date.
